title: Mailbox inside a quoted CSV field
rationale: One property changes from the plain baseline: the carrier is a quoted CSV field. The enclosing double quotes are syntax, so the span covers the mailbox only.

provenance.inference: Quote characters are not atext, so the mailbox ends at the closing quote (project inference from the two cited grammars). Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox at the end of a CRLF-terminated CSV record
rationale: One property changes: the value is followed by CR LF. CR is a record delimiter, not part of the mailbox, so the span stops before it. Texts containing CR are expected to be skipped by line-based carriers.

provenance.inference: CR is not atext, so it cannot extend the mailbox (project inference). Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox between doubled quotes in a CSV field
rationale: One property changes: the value sits next to CSV-escaped double quotes inside a quoted field. The doubling is syntax; the quote is not atext, so the span excludes it.

provenance.inference: The same two grammars as the quoted-field case, with escape adjacency. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox between JSON-escaped quotes
rationale: One property changes: backslash-quote pairs touch the value. Neither backslash nor quotation mark is atext, so the escapes are syntax and excluded from the span.

provenance.inference: Escape characters are not part of the mailbox (project inference). Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox in a JSON document nested inside a JSON string
rationale: One property changes: a second serialization level. The mailbox bytes are unchanged and contiguous; the inner quotes appear as backslash-quote pairs.

provenance.inference: Only one nesting level is authored; deeper levels multiply backslashes and are left open. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox inside a quoted logfmt value
rationale: One property changes: a logfmt key=value line with a quoted value. logfmt has no standards-body specification recorded here, so only the mailbox grammar is cited and the carrier syntax is project inference.

provenance.inference: The closing quote and the following space are not atext. The logfmt quoting convention is not backed by a cited source. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox with a percent-encoded at sign in a query value
rationale: One property changes: the at sign is written %40. The decoded value is the baseline mailbox, but the raw text has no at sign, so what a text-level expectation means (decoded value, raw span, or no match) is open. No span is authored.

reasons: The decoded octets equal a reserved mailbox, but the raw text is not a mailbox in the RFC 5322 grammar.
Which representation an expectation addresses (raw bytes or decoded value) is a project decision; a span over the encoded token would assume one.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A project decision on whether expectations address raw text spans or decoded values, with a documented span convention for decoded representations.

provenance.inference: Identity valid refers to the decoded value only (project inference). Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox with a JSON unicode-escaped at sign
rationale: One property changes: the at sign is written as a six-character JSON escape. A JSON parser yields the baseline mailbox; the raw text is not a mailbox. Same open question as the percent-encoded twin, in a different serialization. No span is authored.

reasons: JSON allows any character to be escaped, so the encoded form is legitimate and decodes to the baseline mailbox.
Raw-text versus decoded-value scope is undecided, as for the percent-encoded twin.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: The same project decision on raw-text versus decoded-value scope.

provenance.inference: Identity valid refers to the decoded value only (project inference). Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox followed by an ideographic full stop
rationale: One property changes: sentence punctuation is U+3002 instead of an ASCII period. Extended atext admits non-ASCII characters, so the grammar alone does not separate punctuation from address, and the domain end is unclear. No span is authored; this is a deferred ambiguity, not an expectation.

reasons: RFC 6531 extends atext with non-ASCII characters in the local part, but this character follows the domain, where the grammar is a different question.
An IDNA treatment of this character as a dot was not read, so whether it belongs to the domain is unresolved.
The ASCII-period counterpart is already an authored positive with the period excluded.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: Reading the IDNA mapping rules for U+3002 and a project convention for sentence punctuation after a mailbox.

provenance.inference: Unresolved by design; recorded so the question is not lost. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Phone number inside a quoted CSV field
rationale: One property changes from the plain baseline: the carrier is a quoted CSV field. The quotes are syntax; the span covers the number only. The value uses the fictional 555-01xx range.

provenance.inference: The quoted-field claim is from RFC 4180; the number's reserved status is from the existing range claim. That the carrier does not change the number is project inference. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: International phone number with an unescaped plus in a query value
rationale: One property changes: the plus sign is not percent-encoded. Form parsing reads a plus as a space, so the leading plus of the number can be lost. Whether the raw plus-prefixed token or the parsed value is the expectation target is open. No span is authored.

reasons: Per form parsing the plus becomes a space, so the parsed value has no plus; the raw text still reads as an E.164-style number.
A producer may have intended a literal plus without encoding it; the text alone does not say.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A project decision on raw versus parsed targets and whether a lost plus changes identity.

provenance.inference: Identity is left not-established because the plus is a formatting character and the digits alone do not settle it (project inference). Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.
